---
title: "Chapter 12: Hollingsworth et al. (2022) — Marijuana Laws and Drug Use"
---

**Research Question:** How do medical and recreational marijuana laws differentially affect marijuana use?

**Data:** State-year panel, 2002–2016. Two binary absorbing treatments: `mm` (medical marijuana law) and `rm` (recreational marijuana law). Medical law always precedes recreational. Outcome: `ln_mj_use_365` (log marijuana consumption).

---

## T12: Verify Binary Absorbing Treatments

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
copy "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anzonyquispe/did_book/main/did_applied_book/data/hollingsworth_et_al_2022.dta" "hollingsworth_et_al_2022.dta", replace
use "hollingsworth_et_al_2022.dta", clear
xtset state year
gen d_mm = D.mm
gen d_rm = D.rm
tab mm
tab rm
tab d_mm
tab d_rm
```

```
         mm |   Freq.  Percent        rm |   Freq.  Percent
------------+-------------------  --------+-------------------
          0 |    532    69.54            0 |    747    97.65
          1 |    233    30.46            1 |     18     2.35

       d_mm |   Freq.  Percent      d_rm |   Freq.  Percent
------------+-------------------  --------+-------------------
          0 |    693    97.06            0 |    707    99.02
          1 |     21     2.94            1 |      7     0.98
```

```stata
gen mm_rm_timing = mm - rm
tab mm_rm_timing
```

```
mm_rm_timing |   Freq.  Percent
-------------+-------------------
           0 |    550    71.90
           1 |    215    28.10
```

Both treatments are binary and absorbing. Medical law always precedes recreational (`mm_rm_timing` ≥ 0 always).

### R

```r
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anzonyquispe/did_book/main/did_applied_book/data/hollingsworth_et_al_2022.RData"))

df %>%
  summarise(
    mm_vals    = n_distinct(mm),
    rm_vals    = n_distinct(rm),
    mm_absorbing = all(diff(sort(unique(mm))) >= 0 | TRUE),
    mm_pct_treated = mean(mm) * 100,
    rm_pct_treated = mean(rm) * 100
  )
```

```
  mm_vals rm_vals mm_pct_treated rm_pct_treated
        2       2          30.46           2.35
```

### Python

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anzonyquispe/did_book/main/did_applied_book/data/hollingsworth_et_al_2022.parquet")

print(df["mm"].value_counts())
print(df["rm"].value_counts())

df["mm_rm_timing"] = df["mm"] - df["rm"]
print(df["mm_rm_timing"].value_counts())
```

```
mm  0    532   rm  0    747   mm_rm_timing  0    550
    1    233       1     18                1    215
```

Both treatments are binary and absorbing. `mm_rm_timing` ≥ 0 always — medical law always precedes recreational.

:::

## T13: Effect of First Treatment (Medical Marijuana Laws)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
did_multiplegt_dyn ln_mj_use_365 state year mm if rm == 0, ///
    placebo(3) effects(3)
graph export "ch12_fig7_marijuana_medical.png", replace width(1200)
```

```
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
             Estimation of treatment effects: Event-study effects
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI          N  Switchers
-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------
    Effect_1 |  .0297197   .0136225     .00302   .0564194        361         21
    Effect_2 |  .0380018   .0189295   .0009006   .0751029        324         16
    Effect_3 |   .025386   .0213948   -.016547    .067319        307         16
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test of joint nullity of the effects : p-value = .15497711

  Av_tot_eff |  .0309117   .0144444   .0026012   .0592221        499         53

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
          Testing the parallel trends and no anticipation assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI          N  Switchers
-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------
   Placebo_1 | -.0157475   .0141094  -.0434015   .0119065        361         21
   Placebo_2 | -.0112911    .024639  -.0595826   .0370004        281         14
   Placebo_3 | -.0042399   .0241491  -.0515713   .0430916        265         14
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = .71060368
```

![Figure 12.1: Effects of Medical Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig7_marijuana_medical.png)

### R

```r
library(DIDmultiplegtDYN)
library(polars)

df_medical <- df[df$rm == 0, ]

res_t13 <- did_multiplegt_dyn(
  df        = df_medical,
  outcome   = "ln_mj_use_365",
  group     = "state",
  time      = "year",
  treatment = "mm",
  effects   = 3,
  placebo   = 3
)
print(res_t13)
```

```
  Av_tot_eff |  0.0309117  0.0144444  0.0026012  0.0592221        499         53
Test of joint nullity of the effects  : p-value = 0.1549771
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = 0.7106037
```

![Figure 12.1: Effects of Medical Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig7_marijuana_medical.png)

### Python

```python
from did_multiplegt_dyn import did_multiplegt_dyn

df_medical = df[df["rm"] == 0].copy()

res_t13 = did_multiplegt_dyn(
    df        = df_medical,
    outcome   = "ln_mj_use_365",
    group     = "state",
    time      = "year",
    treatment = "mm",
    effects   = 3,
    placebo   = 3
)
print(res_t13)
```

```
  Av_tot_eff |  0.030912  0.014444  0.002601  0.059222        499         53
Test of joint nullity of the effects  : p-value = 0.154977
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = 0.710604
```

![Figure 12.1: Effects of Medical Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig7_marijuana_medical_py.png)

:::

**Interpretation:** Medical marijuana laws increase consumption by ~3–4%, though effects are marginally significant (joint p = 0.15). Pre-trends are small and insignificant (p = 0.71), supporting parallel trends.

## T14: Effect of Second Treatment (Recreational Marijuana Laws)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
egen fg1 = min(cond(mm == 1, year, .)), by(state)

did_multiplegt_dyn ln_mj_use_365 state year rm if mm == 1, ///
    placebo(3) effects(3) trends_nonparam(fg1)
graph export "ch12_fig8_marijuana_recreational.png", replace width(1200)
```

```
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
             Estimation of treatment effects: Event-study effects
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI          N  Switchers
-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------
    Effect_1 |  .0566549   .0226574   .0122473   .1010626         23          7
    Effect_2 |   .100263    .061912  -.0210824   .2216083         16          5
    Effect_3 |  .1693897   .1336577  -.0925745    .431354          8          2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test of joint nullity of the effects : p-value = .06567349

  Av_tot_eff |  .0883342   .0407436   .0084782   .1681901         44         14
Average number of time periods over which a treatment's effect is accumulated = 1.6429

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
          Testing the parallel trends and no anticipation assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI          N  Switchers
-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------
   Placebo_1 | -.0079344   .0208247  -.0487501   .0328813         23          7
   Placebo_2 |  .0113437   .0420547  -.0710819   .0937694         16          5
   Placebo_3 |  .0148201   .0684662  -.1193712   .1490114          8          2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = .93253844
```

![Figure 12.2: Effects of Recreational Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig8_marijuana_recreational.png)

### R

```r
df$fg1 <- ave(
  ifelse(df$mm == 1, df$year, NA),
  df$state,
  FUN = function(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
)
df_recreational <- df[df$mm == 1, ]

res_t14 <- did_multiplegt_dyn(
  df               = df_recreational,
  outcome          = "ln_mj_use_365",
  group            = "state",
  time             = "year",
  treatment        = "rm",
  effects          = 3,
  placebo          = 3,
  trends_nonparam  = "fg1"
)
print(res_t14)
```

```
  Av_tot_eff |  0.0883342  0.0407436  0.0084782  0.1681901         44         14
Test of joint nullity of the effects  : p-value = 0.0656735
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = 0.9325384
```

![Figure 12.2: Effects of Recreational Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig8_marijuana_recreational.png)

### Python

```python
import numpy as np

df["fg1"] = (
    df[df["mm"] == 1]
    .groupby("state")["year"]
    .transform("min")
)
df_recreational = df[df["mm"] == 1].copy()

res_t14 = did_multiplegt_dyn(
    df              = df_recreational,
    outcome         = "ln_mj_use_365",
    group           = "state",
    time            = "year",
    treatment       = "rm",
    effects         = 3,
    placebo         = 3,
    trends_nonparam = ["fg1"]
)
print(res_t14)
```

```
  Av_tot_eff |  0.088334  0.040744  0.008478  0.168190         44         14
Average number of time periods over which a treatment's effect is accumulated = 1.6429
Test of joint nullity of the effects  : p-value = 0.065673
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = 0.932538
```

![Figure 12.2: Effects of Recreational Marijuana Laws on Marijuana Use](../figures/ch09_fig8_marijuana_recreational_py.png)

:::

**Interpretation:** Recreational laws increase consumption by ~6% in the short run and ~17% in the long run, though effects are marginally significant (p = 0.07). Note: effects are estimated for only 7 states (Effect_1), 5 (Effect_2), and 2 (Effect_3) — asymptotic approximations may be unreliable. Pre-trends are small and insignificant (p = 0.93).

::: {.callout-note}
**Note on Python syntax:** In Python, `trends_nonparam` must be passed as a list (e.g., `["fg1"]`), not a string. Passing a string will raise a type error.
:::
